title: Clopen system projection is the specified direct-image unit
statement: Let $C_1\leftarrow C_2\leftarrow\cdots$ be any inverse sequence of commutative rings. For a scheme $X$, use its small pro-etale site and the ordinary and derived strict semilinear module-system operations of [def-sp-varying-ring-operations], with the simultaneous models of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Let $s:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion with closed image and let $c:X\setminus s(U)\hookrightarrow X$ be its complementary open. Write $J_s\dashv P_s\dashv S_s$, with open unit $u_s$ and direct-image unit $\eta_s$. Let $t_s:J_s\to S_s$ be the $P_s\dashv S_s$ transpose of $u_s^{-1}:P_sJ_s\to1$, and let $\pi_s:1\to J_sP_s$ be identity on the selected clopen component and zero on its complement [def-sp-varying-ring-proper-open-arrows]. Then $t_s$ is invertible and $(t_sP_s)\circ\pi_s=\eta_s$. Under the open-unit identification, $P_s\pi_s=1$, while $P_c\pi_s=0$. All comparisons are transformations on the whole system derived category, natural in the coefficient sequence and induced by the corresponding ordinary section formulas.

source.place: Tag 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero), specialized to a disjoint clopen decomposition on the ringed sequence site; agent-written extension to arbitrary coefficient systems

proof.text: Write $P^0=s^*_{\bullet}$, $J^0=s_{!,\bullet}$ and $E=s_{*,\bullet}$ for the ordinary system functors. For every pro-etale test object $H\to X$, put $H_U=H\times_XU$ and $H_C=H\times_X(X\setminus s(U))$. The two open immersions form a covering in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]: every affine open of $H$ is quasi-compact and hence covered by finitely many affine opens in these two pieces. Their intersection is empty. The sheaf equalizer of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], including the empty covering of the empty object, gives $M_n(H)=M_n(H_U)\times M_n(H_C)$ with $M_n(\varnothing)=0$. Restriction maps and scalar actions preserve both factors [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Every semilinear transition of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] preserves them too: restriction commutes with the transition and $t(ax)=\phi_n(a)t(x)$. Thus this is a decomposition of actual ordinary systems, natural in $M$ and $H$.

source.place: Tag 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero), disjoint-cover specialization; the two-factor calculation is the sheaf axiom

proof.text: By the direct-image section formula in [def-sp-varying-ring-operations], $(EF)_n(H)=F_n(H_U)$, and $P^0EF=F$ canonically. For a system map $a:F\to P^0M$, the maps $x\mapsto(a(x),0)$ define $EF\to M$ under step 1's decomposition. Conversely, restrict any map $EF\to M$ to objects over $U$. These operations are inverse: over $H_C$ the source is zero, and over $H_U$ its map is the restricted one; sheaf uniqueness identifies the map over $H$. The formulas commute with all transitions and are linear over the section-ring restrictions. They give $E\dashv P^0$ with unit $1\to P^0E$ the identity. The specified adjunction $J^0\dashv P^0$ of [def-sp-varying-ring-operations] therefore gives a unique natural isomorphism $\kappa:J^0\xrightarrow{\sim}E$ carrying its unit $u^0$ to this identity: $P^0\kappa\circ u^0=1$. Explicitly the inverse is the adjunct of $u^0$; each composite is the identity because its adjunct is the same unit.

source.place: Tag 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero), adjunction; explicit clopen section formula and uniqueness of its left adjoint

proof.text: The ordinary right adjunction $P^0\dashv E$ in [def-sp-varying-ring-operations] has counit $P^0EF\to F$ the identity and unit $q_M:M\to EP^0M$ given on sections by $(x,y)\mapsto x$. Indeed the right-adjunction correspondence sends $b:P^0M\to F$ to the map $(x,y)\mapsto b(x)$, and sends this map back to $b$. Hence the right transpose of $\kappa$ is $P^0\kappa=(u^0)^{-1}$; $\kappa$ is exactly the specified ordinary open-to-direct-image arrow of [def-sp-varying-ring-proper-open-arrows], rather than an unspecified isomorphism. Put $\pi^0=(\kappa P^0)^{-1}q$. It is identity on $U$ and zero on the complement. Therefore $(\kappa P^0)\pi^0=q=\eta^0$, $P^0\pi^0=u^0_{P^0(-)}$, and $c^*_{\bullet}\pi^0=0$. The last equality has zero target since $(EP^0M)_n(H)=M_n(\varnothing)=0$ for $H$ over the complement.

source.place: Tag 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero), its adjunction and canonical comparison; direct computation of the two ordinary units

proof.text: The ordinary $J^0$ and $P^0$ are exact by [def-sp-varying-ring-operations]; step 2's isomorphism implies $E$ is exact as well. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] to $E$: its total unbounded right derived functor is computed on every complex by termwise $E$, so $S_s=RE\cong D(E)$. The categories are abelian (indeed Grothendieck) by [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], and all three functors are additive. Thus [lem-sfb-exact-derived-natural-iso] localizes $\kappa$ to an isomorphism $D(J^0)\to D(E)$. Under $J_s=D(J^0)$ and $P_s=D(P^0)$, localize the two exact adjunctions with their specified units and counits as in [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction]. The adjunctions supplied by [def-sp-varying-ring-operations] are induced from these ordinary adjunctions, so the exact-functor comparison with $RE$ carries the localized unit and counit to $\eta_s,\varepsilon_s$. Explicitly, if $P^0K\to I$ is a K-injective resolution, the derived unit is $K\xrightarrow{q}EP^0K\to EI$; the second arrow is the canonical exact-derived isomorphism. Naturality of $q$ identifies this with its termwise localization. The counit follows by the same adjunction correspondence and its triangle identities.

source.place: Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor), all complexes compute the derived functor; exact adjunction and natural-isomorphism localization

proof.text: By [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction], the right transpose of localized $\kappa$ is the localization of $\varepsilon^0\circ P^0\kappa=(u^0)^{-1}$; hence it is $u_s^{-1}$. The bijection of the specified adjunction $P_s\dashv S_s$ identifies localized $\kappa$ with exactly $t_s$, proving its invertibility. Localize the ordinary identities of step 3 to obtain $(t_sP_s)\circ D(\pi^0)=\eta_s$, $P_sD(\pi^0)=u_sP_s$ and $P_cD(\pi^0)=0$. Here $D(\pi^0)$ denotes the localized termwise transformation. It is the specified component projection $\pi_s$: on every ordinary system and in every cochain degree its formula is identity on the chosen component and zero on the other. The simultaneous models of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] use those very ordinary maps. Consequently $P_s\pi_s=1$ under the open unit, as asserted. These are identities localized from maps of whole complexes of systems, not inferred from equality after evaluating a derived system at each $n$.

source.place: Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor); termwise localization of the explicit identities of steps 2-3

proof.text: For naturality, let $C_\bullet\to D_\bullet$ be a compatible map of coefficient sequences. Restriction of scalars leaves pairs, $x\mapsto(x,0)$ and $(x,y)\mapsto x$ unchanged. For extension of scalars, step 1 identifies the system categories with the product of the two component categories: the inverse sends $(F,G)$ to $s_{*,\bullet}F\oplus c_{*,\bullet}G$, with the two inverse identities given by the same section decompositions. A balanced bilinear map out of two such pairs is precisely a pair of balanced bilinear maps, so the universal property of tensor computes tensor and coefficient extension separately on both components. A complex in this product is acyclic exactly when its two components are, and hence is K-flat exactly when both components are K-flat. Thus the K-flat scalar-extension models of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] also act componentwise. Tensoring the displayed identities and zero maps gives identities and zero maps on these actual models, so all comparison squares commute before localization and descend to the derived categories. All maps are natural in the coefficient sequence and in the systems. No flatness of a coefficient transition, cartesianness of a system, or boundedness of a complex has been used.

source.place: Tag 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero), sectionwise identity/zero calculation; agent extension to coefficient change on the ringed sequence site

proof_origin.place: Tag 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero) and Tag 03DJ (lemma-extension-by-zero-exact), clopen disjoint-cover argument; derived.tex Tag 015F. The semilinear-system extension and map normalization are written out here.
